title: Knee Cracking, Clicking or Grinding: Is It Arthritis?
metaDescription: Does your knee crack, click or grind? Most knee noises are harmless, but with pain or swelling they can signal arthritis. Know when to worry.
intro: Most knee clicks and cracks are harmless, especially if there is no pain, swelling or locking. But a grinding or crunching feeling together with pain can be a sign of knee arthritis. The noise alone is not the problem; what comes with it matters.

sections.heading: Is a cracking knee a sign of arthritis?
sections.body: Not on its own. Painless clicking or popping is common. If the noise comes without pain, swelling or catching, it is usually nothing to worry about. If it comes with pain, it is worth having the knee examined.

sections.heading: What does arthritis grinding feel like?
sections.body: Versus Arthritis describes it as a creaking, crunching or grinding feeling when you move the joint. The NHS also lists a grating or crackling sound as a symptom. In arthritis it usually comes with stiffness, pain on moving and sometimes swelling.

sections.heading: When is knee noise a warning sign?
sections.body: See a doctor if the noise comes with pain, swelling, the knee giving way, or if the knee locks or catches. Locking after a twisting injury can mean a torn cartilage pad (meniscus) and should be checked.

sections.heading: Will exercise make my knee cracking worse?
sections.body: No. The right exercise strengthens the muscles that support the knee. Not moving tends to make stiffness and pain worse. Start gently and build up.

sections.heading: What can I do about a noisy knee?
sections.body: If it is painless, nothing is needed. If it is painful, we usually start with medicines to settle the pain, then exercises to strengthen the thigh muscles, and add other treatments only if needed.

faqs.q: Why does my knee crack when I stand up?
faqs.a: Painless clicking is usually harmless. Pain or swelling alongside it is the reason to get checked.

faqs.q: Is knee cracking bad for you?
Can cracking knees lead to arthritis?
faqs.a: Noise alone does not mean arthritis is coming. Arthritis is mainly linked to age, past injury, family history and weight.

faqs.q: Should I stop squatting if my knee cracks?
faqs.a: If it is painless, there is no need to stop. If squatting hurts, reduce it and have the knee checked.

faqs.q: Do I need an X-ray for knee noises?
faqs.a: Not for painless clicking. If there is pain, swelling or locking, an examination and X-ray help.
